page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c40g1.10xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. The host is configured with 40 dedicated vCPUs sourced from 20 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores running at 2.5 GHz. System memory totals 155 GB, providing 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware-based acceleration is delivered through a single NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance includes a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile and contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disk access.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear contrast between CPU execution profiles and GPU acceleration capabilities. Single-core processor throughput is weak, as reflected in lower-tier single-threaded compression benchmarks and a Geekbench single-core score of 934. Conversely, multi-threaded operations maintain middle-tier performance, marked by a PassMark CPU score of 27,268.93 and a stress-ng multi-core measurement of 29,537.99. Memory bandwidth reaches 99.06 GB/sec under uncached read conditions. The primary performance highlight is machine learning prompt evaluation, achieving top-tier speeds exceeding 1,129 tokens per second on 7B models and over 8,345 tokens per second on lightweight 135M architectures.

Qualitatively, the server provides an efficient resource footprint for deep learning inference and media processing, pairing an energy-efficient accelerator with high host memory. The platform is constrained by older CPU per-core processing limits and a lack of local high-speed NVMe storage. Workloads best aligned with this configuration include small-to-medium LLM inference up to 7B parameters, image transformation, parallel data processing, and GPU-assisted enterprise microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c40g1.10xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance featuring 40 dedicated vCPUs on 20 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 155 GB of system RAM. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. Networking features a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while local disk storage is omitted, relying on attached cloud volumes. Benchmark results highlight modest single-thread CPU performance balanced by average multi-core throughput and top-tier prompt processing speeds on small to medium-scale language models. The instance demonstrates qualitative cost efficiency for model inference workloads, image processing, and distributed GPU compute tasks that require sizable host system memory but remain constrained within the 16 GB GPU memory ceiling.
